issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify Animal.messageOnFeed() as returning a String, but the solution implements messageOnFeed() to return a FeedResponse object. This return-type divergence is structural: students following the specification will implement messageOnFeed(): String, while the provided solution (and its helper FeedResponse class) use a different type, causing confusion and incompatible expectations for printing and tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the specification and implementation. Either: (A) Update the problem statement/UML to state that Animal.messageOnFeed() returns a FeedResponse (and document the FeedResponse class and why it is used), or (B) Modify the solution to have Animal.messageOnFeed() return a String (and remove or refactor FeedResponse) so the code and UML match the original exercise intent.

issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify Animal.messageOnFeed() should return a String, but the solution changes the method signature to return a FeedResponse object (introducing a new FeedResponse class). This creates a mismatch between the exercise specification and the provided solution: students will expect to implement messageOnFeed() returning String (and the template text places messageOnFeed() return values directly into printed verses), while the solution uses an object whose toString() happens to provide the message. This divergence in the return type and the introduction of FeedResponse creates unnecessary cognitive mapping overhead and may confuse students about the expected method signature.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the method signature with the problem statement: change Animal.messageOnFeed() to return String in the solution and update all subclasses (Seal, Pig, Goat) to return the message String directly. Remove or avoid using FeedResponse for messageOnFeed(), or explicitly document the FeedResponse type in the problem statement and UML if keeping it is intentional.
